item.title: Weekend Digest, September 5, 2026
item.description:
Trujillo Times

Saturday, September 5, 2026 — Sunny today, high near 97°F (heat index up to 104°F); overnight low around 74°F. Heat Advisory in effect until 8 PM today.

At a Glance

  • Sunny today, high near 97°F with a heat index up to 104°F; overnight low around 74°F. Heat Advisory in effect until 8 PM today.
  • Nothing scheduled today; three events on the calendar this week, including Wednesday's Companywide Town Hall.
  • Portfolio section unavailable — no holdings configured in DigestConfig.md.
  • Markets swung on renewed U.S.-Iran tension and rising bond yields before rallying Thursday; Nvidia struck its biggest deal ever with a roughly $12.9 billion buyout of Hugging Face, and OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Astra.
  • Barcelona routed Rayo Vallecano 5-2 and Miami blitzed Stanford 45-6 in Darian Mensah's debut; the Vikings had no game, and Barcelona's transfer window closed for the season.
  • The Verge and Uncrate each posted five new items this week, while The Art of Manliness closed out the week with its regular Friday link roundup.

Calendar

Today

Nothing scheduled today.

Week Ahead

  • Wed Sep 9, 1:00 PM — Companywide Town Hall (Microsoft Teams Meeting)
  • Thu Sep 10, 12:00 PM — Bar-B-Clean Brings Lunch!!! (Microsoft Teams Meeting)
  • Sat Sep 12, 11:00 AM — Brunch for Mac and Kate

Newsletters

The Art of Manliness — One new item, the site's regular Friday "Odds & Ends" roundup: a recommendation of Masaki Kobayashi's 1962 samurai film Harakiri, a nod to Wendell Berry's short story "Pray Without Ceasing" from his Fidelity collection following Berry's death at 92, a plug for the Osprey Atmos AG 65 backpack ahead of fall backpacking season, a link to the "Ordinary Abundance" site pairing everyday household items with historical reactions to their invention, and a closing Phillips Brooks quote on refusing to live a "half life."

The Verge — Five new items, but the site blocked automated access to the full articles this run, so only titles can be reported: "Audacity 4 is a complete revamp of the 'world's most popular' audio editor"; "The White House is making arcade games racist"; "GoPro says it's still committed 'to your collective stoke'"; "Roland is getting into generative AI music with Melody Flip"; and "AGI is whatever you want it to be."

Cool Material — Two new items, also blocked from automated access: "The Art of Cocktail Conversation" and "The Luggage Combo for Trips That Mix Business With Leisure."

Uncrate — Five new items: a set of four charity Rolex Cosmograph Daytona watches themed to the seasons, each in a different precious metal with a gem-set dial and diamond-set lugs, with auction proceeds benefiting the Federer Foundation and Re:wild. The Balmuda MoonKettle, a $259 temperature-controlled electric kettle with single-degree precision from 122°F to 212°F, ambient LED lighting, and a 30-minute hold function. A one-off 1953 Cadillac Elegante concept car with a retractable hardtop and Lucite steering wheel, hand-built by Italian coachbuilder Carrozzeria Motto over 30 months and headed to public auction for the first time since it was built. An "Everyday Carry: Utilitarian" roundup pairing a $1,050 Unimatic GMT watch with Gucci sunglasses, a Firebiner multitool, and a James Brand utility knife. And the Plaud One, a $250 wearable AI earbud system with its own cellular eSIM, up to six hours of listening time, and onboard transcription, summarization, and calendar tools.

Earlier this week — already covered in weekday editions:

The Art of Manliness — A Field Guide to 8 Regional Burger Styles; Podcast #1,131: To Change Yourself, Change Your Situation; How My Grandpa Built a Big Life From Little Purposes; How to Make Yourself Easier to Talk To.

Bless This Stuff — Tangent Urban Safari 911; Loop Eclipse Sleep Mask; Pelican PX35 Aegis 35L Creator Backpack; Xeric x Worn & Wound Sector Retrograde Watch; Blakely Island Cabin.

Cool Material — How to Serve Great Cocktails Without Missing Your Own Party; The Summer Edit: 10 Pieces That Make Getting Dressed Ridiculously Easy; Enter to Win a Beach Getaway, On Us; Finding Nature and Nurture in Puerto Vallarta; Black Book: 12 Products Our Editors Loved in August 2026.

News

Stock market

CNBC / Yahoo Finance — Stocks whipsawed through the week: Tuesday's session fell as renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities pushed oil prices higher, before Wednesday's cooling Treasury yields lifted the S&P 500 and Nasdaq roughly 0.5% each. Thursday brought the sharpest move, with the Dow jumping 624 points (1.2%) to 53,686.11 and the S&P and Nasdaq both gaining more than 1%, as Fed Governor Christopher Waller signaled he'd favor holding rates steady barring an inflation surprise. The 10-year Treasury yield still touched 4.818% on Wednesday, its highest since November 2023, after August nonfarm payrolls grew by 162,000 — triple the 53,000 economists expected — and pushed fed-funds futures to price a 58% chance of a rate hike. Friday gave some of the week's gains back, with the Dow closing at 53,414.25, the S&P 500 at 7,718.60, and the Nasdaq at 26,506.99.

Geopolitics

Just Security / Security Council Report — Tension with Iran stayed front and center: President Trump said the U.S. would hit back "hard" after Iranian attacks on bases in Jordan, while downplaying talk of a return to full-scale war and calling Iran a "failed nation." At the UN, France took over the Security Council presidency for September and is expected to bring a vote on renewing Sudan's sanctions regime before it lapses on September 12. Diplomats are also weighing candidates for the next UN Secretary-General amid what analysts describe as rising strain on multilateral institutions. September's calendar still points toward a Xi-Trump summit alongside UN General Assembly, SCO, and BRICS+ meetings, all set against the backdrop of the unresolved U.S.-Iran confrontation.

Technology

Tech Startups / CNBC — Nvidia agreed to its largest deal ever this week, buying AI platform Hugging Face for roughly $12.9 billion in cash plus about $1 billion in retention equity; Hugging Face says its hub will stay open to competing models and chips, though the deal will test how independent it can remain inside Nvidia. Broadcom separately reported AI-chip revenue up 221% year over year, and China's Moonshot AI is reportedly preparing a Hong Kong IPO near a $50 billion valuation. Tesla began running wheel-free Cybercabs on Austin streets and almost immediately drew a federal safety probe. At the G20 Innovation Ministerial in Chapel Hill, member countries endorsed non-binding, U.S.-backed AI policy principles favoring light-touch, sector-specific regulation.

AI

Tech Startups / CNBC — OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Astra this week, rolling it out over several days to paid ChatGPT plans, its API, Azure, and Bedrock, with the company framing the release as the arrival of an "AGI era." Anthropic said Claude worked largely autonomously over 11 days on the Prove2Me platform to produce the first end-to-end, computer-checked proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in the Lean programming language. At the same Chapel Hill summit, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick publicly praised Anthropic, telling the audience "we trust" the lab and that it's "back on the right side" with the administration. Separately, Nvidia researchers reported their Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC model scored 535.4 out of 600 on the IOI 2026 programming olympiad problem set, ahead of the top human contestant's 498.27.

Tech business, startups, and VC

Tech Funding News / Tech Startups — Venture money this week clustered around AI, deeptech, cybersecurity, industrial technology, and biology, with investors pressing founders harder for proof of real customers and commercial traction rather than just growth potential. Biotech drew some of the largest checks: AusperBio Therapeutics closed a $120 million Series C and Elucid raised $55 million in a Series D. Fintech company Félix closed a Series C plus growth-debt package totaling $200 million in equity and $113 million in debt, while smaller rounds went to banking-tech startup Cradlewise ($12 million Series A) and pre-seed cargo-drone startup Outlier Space (roughly $7.35 million).

Golf equipment

GOLF.com / Golf Monthly — Tour Edge unveiled its all-new Exotics Milled Wedge Series this week, built around a three-part "TriGrind Sole" designed for cleaner turf interaction and more versatility around the greens; the wedges arrive at retail and touredge.com on September 14 for $119.99. The launch adds to a busy 2026 club season that has already brought Cobra's Optm driver family, built around peak moment-of-inertia for accuracy, PING's G440 K driver replacing the G430 Max 10K, and Titleist's Vokey SM11 wedges with refined grinds and shaping.

Pokémon investing

TCGIndex — The Pokémon TCG remains the largest single trading-card game within the roughly $8–9 billion global card market, holding an estimated 12% share, and as of September 4 the tracker had 12 of the 14 games it follows trending up on the week. Chase cards — Special Illustration Rares, Immersive Rares, and select vintage sealed product — continue to command premiums even as modern common cards stay oversupplied after The Pokémon Company printed 11.9 billion cards in fiscal 2023–24. Market watchers describe the space as stabilized since its pandemic-era boom and correction, with current guidance favoring graded chase cards and select vintage sealed product over mass-market singles.

Sports

F.C. Barcelona

ESPN — Barcelona survived an early scare to beat Rayo Vallecano 5-2 last Monday, falling behind in the 12th minute to a Sergio Camello finish before Raphinha equalized in the 19th and Lamine Yamal put the hosts ahead in the 21st. Rayo pulled within one when Camello headed home a corner in the 59th, but Barcelona pulled away with a Florian Lejeune own goal, a Raphinha finish off an Anthony Gordon fast break in the 71st, and a stoppage-adjacent Lamine Yamal strike from outside the box in the 90th, assisted by Karim Adeyemi. Lamine Yamal and Raphinha each scored twice in the win.

Minnesota Vikings

No game in window.

  • ESPN / Star Tribune / NFL.com — Minnesota's week was about roster building rather than games: the Vikings trimmed to a 53-man roster, with edge rusher Tyler Batty already lost for the season to a torn ACL suffered in the preseason finale at Denver. The team added 13-year veteran pass rusher Kyle Van Noy to the practice squad, reuniting him with defensive coordinator Brian Flores from their Patriots days, and settled its punter battle in favor of Brett Thorson over veteran Johnny Hekker.

Miami Hurricanes

ESPN / State of The U / Yahoo Sports — Miami opened its season with a 45-6 rout at Stanford behind a spectacular debut from transfer quarterback Darian Mensah, who went 27-of-30 for 401 yards and five touchdowns. Malachi Toney set Miami's single-game receiving record with 12 catches for 234 yards and three touchdowns, including a 47-yard score in the third quarter, while Cooper Barkate added a 34-yard touchdown catch. Miami led 17-0 after the first quarter on two Mensah-to-Toney touchdowns and an Emmet Kenney field goal, and never let Stanford threaten; Jake Weinberg closed the scoring with a 46-yard field goal in the fourth. Stanford managed only two field goals from Emmet Kenney and was outgained badly, with quarterback Davis Warren going 21-of-41 for 214 yards.

Soccer transfer rumors

The summer transfer window closed September 1; with it shut, there are no live rumors to report until the January window opens.

  • Barca Blaugranes — Barcelona's completed window brought in Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi, Gabriel Jesus, and World Cup winner Rodri, while Robert Lewandowski departed for MLS side Chicago Fire at the end of his contract. A deadline-day pursuit of Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez fell apart after Atletico's board cut off talks, and he is set to stay in Madrid at least through January.

Week Ahead

  • Barcelona at Valencia — LaLiga, Sun Sep 6
  • Florida A&M Rattlers at Miami Hurricanes — Sat Sep 11
  • Vikings vs. Green Bay Packers — Sun Sep 13 (regular-season opener)

And Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.1, cutting costs for heavy agentic work by up to 45% and reducing false-positive security flags in Claude Code by about 60%.

item.description:
Trujillo Times

Saturday, August 29, 2026 — Patchy fog then a slight chance of showers and thunderstorms today, high near 88°F; overnight low around 69°F. No active alerts.

At a Glance

  • Patchy fog and a slight chance of showers and thunderstorms today, high near 88°F; overnight low around 69°F. No active alerts.
  • Showroom Meeting at 2pm today; seven more events on the calendar this week, including Bar Incognito next Wednesday evening.
  • Portfolio section unavailable — no holdings configured in DigestConfig.md.
  • Nvidia's blowout earnings lifted markets midweek, but new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech pulled stocks back Friday; all three major indexes still closed the week higher.
  • Barcelona opened LaLiga 2-0 with routs of Elche (5-0) and Athletic Club (2-0); the Vikings dropped both preseason finales with Sunday's roster-cut deadline looming.
  • The Verge and Uncrate each posted five new items this week, including Google burying search further under AI Mode and the EPA's push to let data centers hide air pollution.

Calendar

Today

Showroom Meeting, 2:00 PM (Microsoft Teams Meeting).

Week Ahead

  • Sun Aug 30, All day — Tate Hunter Returning from Europe
  • Sun Aug 30, 9:00 PM — Dialed Fantasy Draft
  • Tue Sep 1, All day — Natalie Anniversary
  • Tue Sep 1, 5:45 PM — Haircut
  • Wed Sep 2, All day — Dad's Return
  • Wed Sep 2, 10:00 AM — Bromic Vendor-Led Training (Microsoft Teams Meeting)
  • Wed Sep 2, 6:00 PM — Bar Incognito

Newsletters

The Art of Manliness — Two new pieces this week: the site's regular link roundup, covering Brett McKay's recommendation of Robert Richardson's biography of philosopher William James, notes from the McKay family's Vermont trip (canoeing, e-biking, mountain hiking, and maple creemees from Tozier's Restaurant in Bethel), praise for Brandon Flowers' new country-tinged solo album Thrasher, a mention of a New York Times essay on how constant self-viewing through mirrors and video calls may be feeding body dysmorphia, and a closing Francis Quarles quote on fasting, walking, and prayer; and a recipe guide for making protein energy balls that taste like cookie dough — a no-bake snack of oats, protein powder, peanut butter, honey, chia seeds, and chocolate chips blended and rolled into about 15 balls.

Palladium — One new piece: "Battling All the Way Home," in which Stephen Pimentel argues that Homer's Odyssey remains essential for understanding governance, identity, and human excellence today, and that readers should engage its "alien" elements — real gods, honor-based ethics, retributive justice — rather than dismissing them or projecting modern values onto them. He reads Odysseus's struggle to recover his name, father, land, and household as a model for modern rootlessness, holding up the hero's cunning, endurance, and memory as virtues a purely compassion-centered ethic doesn't fully supply.

The Verge — Five new items: Google is now automatically expanding AI Overviews at the top of search results for some queries, pushing the traditional link list further down the page, with the company saying the expansion happens "where our systems determine it's most useful." Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told BBC News that Project Helix — previously floated as Microsoft's next singular console — will actually ship as a "family of devices," consistent with Microsoft and AMD's multi-year hardware partnership. Amazon and Best Buy discounted TCL's QM7L mini-LED TV to as low as $797.99 for the 55-inch model, a set with 144Hz refresh, Quantum Dot color, and Google TV. The Trump administration's EPA is moving to scrap a rule requiring public notice before industrial sites, including data centers, can get air-pollution permits, which advocates warn would let developers "issue the permits in secret." And modders extracted an unofficial version of Nvidia's leaked DLSS 5 "Neural Rendering" tech from an early-access build of NBA 2K27 and applied it to games like Control, Skyrim, and Cyberpunk 2077 to add AI-altered facial detail.

Bless This Stuff — Four new items: a 1954 Aston Martin DB2/4 Saloon, one of roughly 565 Mark I units built and reportedly once owned by William Randolph Hearst Jr., now listed on Bring a Trailer with a rebuilt straight-six and an upgraded five-speed manual. The Moft Snap-on Phone Stand & Wallet, a MagSafe accessory combining a two-card wallet, magnetic grip, and an origami-style three-position stand in one slim, 60g attachment. The Norda 001A, a Canadian-made ultra-distance trail shoe with a seamless Dyneema upper and an exclusive Norda x Vibram outsole at $295. And a roundup of 20 microbrand and independent watches, from sub-$750 entry brands like Baltic and Vaer to design-forward names like Unimatic and heritage revivals like Benrus and Fears.

Cool Material — Three new items this week, but the site blocked automated access to the full articles, so only their titles can be reported rather than a real summary: "The Back to School Guide for Guys Who Aren't Going Back to School," "Cool Destination: The Ultimate Puerto Vallarta Guide" (sponsored), and "Asheville Has Range."

Uncrate — Five new items: the Rezvani Beast X, a five-unit hypercar built on a Corvette platform with a twin-turbo 6.2-liter V8 making 1,560 hp and a $500,000 price. A build-it-yourself Maison Alcée x MB&F Nostromo desk clock modeled on the spacecraft from Alien, limited to 50 units at $15,000. An "Everyday Carry: Vivid" roundup pairing a Celine leather wallet with a Naval Watch Co. GMT watch, Oakley Frogskins, and a James Brand carabiner. "The New Southern Style," a $195 coffee-table book pairing Southern-home photography with interviews with the designers pushing the region's look past "magnolias and monograms." And a feature on Charleston's Dewberry hotel, a 155-room Mid-Century Modern property with rates starting at $340 a night.

Earlier this week — already covered in weekday editions:

The Art of Manliness — Podcast #1,130: The Lost Virtue of Thumos (And Why Men Need It); How to Get Back From Vacation; Are You Suffering From Soft Suburban Dad Syndrome? 50 Questions for Self-Examination.

Bless This Stuff — DeLorean EV Conversion Kit; Adidas x Song For The Mute Supernova Rise Sneaker; HiDock P1 AI Voice Recorder; Huckberry Sale on Sale 2026; Kudhva K1 Portable Cabin.

Cool Material — Menswear Staples You Didn't Know Had Golf History; The Luxury Lover's Guide to Puerto Vallarta; It's Time to Upgrade Your Gas Station Lighter.

News

Stock market

CNBC / Bloomberg — Nvidia's fiscal second-quarter report Wednesday blew past expectations — revenue of $96.2 billion, up 106% year over year, and guidance for roughly 70% growth in fiscal 2028 versus the 44% Wall Street had penciled in — sending the stock up nearly 9% and lifting chipmakers Broadcom and Intel alongside it. The rally faded some by Friday after new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, in his first Jackson Hole keynote, called inflation still "uncomfortably high" and signaled the Fed has more work to do, pushing the market-implied odds of a September rate hike from roughly 35% to above 55%. Treasury yields rose in response, with the 10-year near 4.72%, and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each slipped Friday. Even so, all three major indexes closed the week higher — the Dow's first winning week in three — with the S&P up about 0.5%, the Nasdaq up 0.9%, and the Dow near 53,560.

Geopolitics

Al Jazeera / NPR / Kyiv Independent — The Gaza ceasefire looked shakier by week's end: Hamas accused Israel of using "fake pretexts" to keep fighting, Israel threatened a forceful response after Hamas revived incendiary-kite attacks, and the U.S.-backed Board of Peace's Gaza envoy warned a full collapse would be a "point of no return," all following Prime Minister Netanyahu's public rejection of President Trump's 15-point peace plan. In Ukraine, Russia struck warehouse facilities in Kyiv Oblast on Friday, briefly closing a major highway to western Ukraine, while Italy pledged four SAMP/T NG air-defense batteries, Aster 30 interceptor missiles, and seven long-range radars. CIA Director John Ratcliffe made a previously undisclosed trip to Moscow, reportedly prompted by a classified assessment that Vladimir Putin senses U.S. weakness in the stalled peace talks; the Kremlin said Ratcliffe did not meet Putin and called it premature to read anything into the visit. U.S.-mediated negotiations remain stuck over territorial concessions and security guarantees.

Technology

NBC News / ABC News / MacRumors / CNBC — Meta agreed this week to pay up to $16.7 billion settling child-safety claims from a 29-state coalition, and must now add daily time caps and an overnight usage block for teens on Facebook and Instagram, along with stronger age verification and parental controls; the company denies wrongdoing but had faced potential exposure topping $1 trillion had it lost at trial. Apple confirmed hardware chief John Ternus will succeed Tim Cook as CEO on September 1, ending Cook's 15-year run atop the company, the same week Apple announced new Mac mini and Mac Studio models and confirmed a September 9 event expected to unveil a foldable iPhone, iPhone 18 Pro models, and new Apple Watches. And Amazon said it's shutting down Mechanical Turk, its 21-year-old crowdsourced task marketplace, on September 30, citing the rise of AI-era data-labeling firms like Scale AI and Mercor that have taken over its niche.

AI

Bloomberg / CNBC / TIME — Anthropic committed roughly $45 billion over six years to UK firm Nscale for about 460 megawatts of data-center capacity at a planned West Virginia campus running on Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin chips, days after Microsoft reportedly exited as the project's anchor tenant. TIME reported OpenAI is resetting strategy under Sam Altman — winding down its Sora video app, a Disney partnership, and the standalone Atlas browser to refocus resources — amid reporting that Anthropic has overtaken it in annualized revenue and private valuation; OpenAI is also retiring the DALL-E model from ChatGPT on Sunday and cut its GPT-5.6 API pricing by more than 20%. It was a financial and infrastructure week for AI rather than a research one — no major new frontier model shipped, but Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate was reported to have passed $65 billion, with investors reportedly eyeing a roughly $2 trillion IPO valuation this fall.

Tech business, startups, and VC

TechCrunch — AI personal-assistant startup Instinct raised a $250 million Series B led by Index Ventures and Benchmark at a $2.5 billion valuation — up from $50 million just months ago — for a product that manages tasks like email, calendars, and travel over text and voice. Stability AI, maker of Stable Diffusion, raised $76 million with backing from Universal Music Group, Sony Music Group, Warner Music Group, and Electronic Arts, while AI robotics startup General Intuition was in talks for a $6 billion valuation as it expands from gaming AI into robotics. And India's Airbound raised a $37 million Series A, led by Greenoaks, for autonomous cargo drones it's positioning as an alternative to trucking.

Golf equipment

CNN / GOLF.com / MyGolfSpy — Callaway severed ties with YouTube golf group Good Good Golf this week after pulling a co-branded driver ad that showed a man shoving a woman to the ground; the company completed an internal review, tightened its ad-approval process, and pledged $1 million to organizations combating violence against women, while Good Good separately stepped back from a PGA Tour title-sponsorship deal. On the gear side, PING expanded its high-MOI Scottsdale TEC putter line with two new mallets, the TEC Ketsch 4 and TEC Ally Blue H. And at the Tour Championship in Atlanta, GolfWRX flagged putter swaps among the 30 FedExCup finalists, including Tommy Fleetwood again gaming the model he won with in 2025 and Alex Fitzpatrick switching to a new Odyssey.

Pokémon investing

PokeGuardian / PokéBeach — The Pokémon World Championships kicked off in San Francisco this weekend at Moscone Center, with finals moving to Chase Center and the new "Pitch Black" set legal for play, drawing heavy secondary coverage of Worlds-tied merchandise. On the retail side, two new tin products hit shelves Friday: an Ascended Heroes Tin at $21.99 featuring Mega Feraligatr ex, Mega Meganium ex, and Mega Emboar ex, and a Mega Forces Tin with alt-art Mega Darkrai ex, Mega Dragonite ex, and Mega Zeraora ex. The broader market held roughly flat, with the tracked index near $987,263 as of August 21 — up 0.2% for the week and 1.8% for the month — and Destined Rivals chase cards like Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex (above $376) and Cynthia's Garchomp ex (above $237) still the top movers, with no single-card blowout sale reported this week.

Sports

F.C. Barcelona

ESPN / Barca Blaugranes — Barcelona opened its LaLiga campaign with two comfortable wins this week, thrashing Elche 5-0 last Sunday and beating Athletic Club 2-0 in Wednesday's home opener at a reopened Camp Nou. Raphinha was the standout at Elche, converting a 14th-minute penalty and later setting up Karim Adeyemi before adding a goal of his own, with Fermin Lopez capping the rout with a brace late on; Raphinha then opened the scoring against Athletic Club in the 37th minute off a Pedri through ball, with Fermin Lopez sealing it in the 82nd. The only scare of the week came when Gavi went down clutching his surgically repaired knee during the Elche match — medical tests found only a bruise, and he's already back in full training. Barcelona sits 2-0-0 to start the season.

Minnesota Vikings

ESPN / Star Tribune / Heavy.com — The Vikings closed out the preseason with two lopsided losses, falling 13-3 to Baltimore last Saturday and 34-6 at Denver on Friday, with backups doing the passing since Kyler Murray was already locked in as the Week 1 starter. Denver's Sam Ehlinger torched Minnesota's defense for 233 yards and three touchdown passes, including an 88-yard strike to Justin Joly, while Minnesota managed only two Will Reichard field goals in the finale. The results matter less than Sunday's 5 p.m. deadline to cut from roughly 90 players to a 53-man roster: wide receiver Jeshaun Jones will serve a three-game suspension starting on cutdown day, quarterback J.J. McCarthy was banged up with an ankle injury against Baltimore, and rookie tackle Caleb Tiernan and safety Theo Jackson are both working toward being ready for the September 13 opener against Green Bay.

Miami Hurricanes

No Hurricanes game or notable team news this week; the season opener is September 5 at Stanford.

Soccer transfer rumors

Sky Sports / Goal.com / Barca Blaugranes — Barcelona's move for Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez collapsed this week after Atletico's board issued a statement ending negotiations over what it called a lack of professional conduct; Alvarez was booed by his own fans in a 2-2 draw with Villarreal, and Arsenal has since emerged as an alternative destination after Atletico's director met with the London club. With the window closing Tuesday, Barcelona is expected to let Alejandro Balde, Marc Casado, and Hector Fort leave before the deadline.

Week Ahead

Today

Nothing scheduled today.

Newsletters

The Art of Manliness — One new piece, a self-examination quiz on "Soft Suburban Dad Syndrome": fifty questions meant to check whether comfort and routine have quietly eroded discipline, ambition, and physical vitality in middle age.

The Verge — Four new items: humanoid robots at a robotics competition reportedly broke Usain Bolt's 100-meter sprint record. A running explainer tracks all the news and trailers for Grand Theft Auto VI, alongside a column arguing the game already exists in its own cultural universe ahead of release. Geopolitics

Technology

AI

Tech business, startups, and VC

Nothing notable today.

Nothing notable today.
